ayahOccurrences.text: وَمَا كَانَ صَلَاتُهُمْ عِندَ ٱلْبَيْتِ إِلَّا مُكَآءً وَتَصْدِيَةً ۚ فَذُوقُوا۟ ٱلْعَذَابَ بِمَا كُنتُمْ تَكْفُرُونَ
ayahOccurrences.highlightedHtml: وَمَا كَانَ صَلَاتُهُمْ عِندَ ٱلْبَيْتِ إِلَّا مُكَآءً وَتَصْدِيَةً ۚ فَذُوقُوا۟ ٱلْعَذَابَ بِمَا كُنتُمْ تَكْفُرُونَ

lexSnapshot.wordGrammar: accusative feminine indefinite (form II) verbal noun
lexSnapshot.derivativeNote: وَتَصْدِيَةً is in the derivative form: تَصْدية
lexSnapshot.rootDefinitionHtml:
ص/د/ى   ṣ–d–y intense thirst, to become thirsty; clapping of the hands, echo; to soothe, to coax; to endeavour; human corpse, skull.

Of this root, 2 forms occur 1 time each in the Qur’an:
تَصَدّى taṣaddā and تَصْدية taṣdiyatun.
lexSnapshot.mainDefinitionHtml:
تَصْدية taṣdiyatan [v. n.] clapping of the hands

(8:35) وَمَا كَانَ صَلاَتُهُمْ عِنْدَ الْبَيْتِ إِلاَّ مُكَاءً وَتَصْدِيَةً their prayer at the House is nothing but a whistling and a clapping of hands.

entries.label: تَصَدَّى
entries.definitionHtml:
تَصَدَّى taṣaddā [imperf. of v. V (with the prefix ﺘ elided), intrans.] to accost, to confront, to give full attention

(80:5–6) أَمَّا مَنِ اسْتَغْنَى فَأَنْتَ لَهُ تَصَدَّى as for the self-satisfied one (i.e., one who has no need [for God, for you [Prophet] or for the Truth]), you give full attention to him.
